newsitem.title: USA: Massport plans Q2 bond sale, picks new syndicate.
newsitem.headline: Massport plans Q2 bond sale, picks new syndicate.

text.p: Massachusetts Port Authority said Friday it plans to sell $200 million to $250 million of bonds in the second quarter, adding that the exact size of the sale hinges on finalizing a capital plan.

The authority, which also selected a new syndicate at a board meeting on Thursday, plans to have the six-member team handle another two bond sales in addition to the ones announced for the second quarter.
But it has yet to decide whether both of these offerings will be in 1997, or whether one will be in 1998, explained David Shapiro, director of business management and budget.

The new syndicate, whose members will rotate, will be led by Bear Stearns, Lehman Brothers and PaineWebber. Goldman, Sachs, which formerly held this slot, was not chosen for any position on the new syndicate.
The new co-managers are Artemis, Smith Barney and Tucker Anthony, Shapiro said, explaining that M.R. Beale & Co also was not reappointed.

While the new syndicate has six members, it is unlikely The Authority initially advertized its second quarter bond sale at around $170 million, but the capital plan identified bigger needs, Massport officials said, adding it also was possible a refunding would be included.
